sources_consulted: https://docs.chain.link/cre/release-notes — CRE release notes, CLI v1.28.0 2026-07-30 [A1]

primitives.name: CRE Triggers
primitives.can: Start a workflow on a cron schedule, HTTP request, or on-chain event
primitives.cant: Not a general scheduler for off-chain apps; trigger types fixed to cron/HTTP/log event
primitives.load_bearing_for: Continuous/periodic re-screening (e.g. daily sanctions re-check, renewal re-KYC) — the 'fails-closed, continuously' legal requirement

primitives.name: CRE HTTP (consensus)
primitives.can: Call any external API from every DON node and reach consensus on the result; verified off-chain data on-chain
primitives.cant: Each node hits the API (rate-limit/cost multiplied by node count); non-deterministic APIs break consensus
primitives.load_bearing_for: DON-consensus verification of a legal data source (OFAC SDN, GLEIF LEI, land registry, court record) — the trust layer that makes the output defensible to a judge

primitives.name: CRE Confidential HTTP (enclave)
primitives.can: Call APIs from inside a secure enclave, injecting secrets, keeping credentials + responses hidden from node operators; optional response encryption
primitives.cant: Enclave adds latency/complexity; still limited to HTTP-reachable sources
primitives.load_bearing_for: Privacy-preserving KYC/PII handling (screen a party without leaking their identity on-chain) — legal data-minimisation / GDPR angle

primitives.name: CRE EVM Read & Write (consensus)
primitives.can: Read contract state and write consensus-verified results to Ethereum/Base/Arbitrum and other EVM chains
primitives.cant: Write cadence/gas bound by target chain; not sub-second
primitives.load_bearing_for: Writing the DON-signed compliance verdict / attestation on-chain as the immutable audit record

primitives.name: CRE Solana Read & Write
primitives.can: Read Solana account/program state; write verified results via Keystone Forwarder (Mainnet + Devnet)
primitives.cant: Not the native target for an EVM-first legal build; adds a second runtime
primitives.load_bearing_for: NOT load-bearing for this EVM-centric build (flagged) — only relevant if a Solana receipt is wanted (cf. Debate Desk)

primitives.name: CRE SDKs + CLI (Go/TypeScript)
primitives.can: Code-first workflow authoring in Go or TS, local simulation, deploy, and execution-observability commands (CLI v1.28.0, 2026-07-30); Developer Assistant MCP server for IDE
primitives.cant: New tooling — smaller community/example corpus than Solidity; workflow debugging less mature
primitives.load_bearing_for: The entire CRE-bounty build surface; TS SDK pairs with a Next.js lawyer-facing frontend

primitives.name: Dami/leash asset stack (EVM)
primitives.can: Solidity contract depth, calldata decode, Permit2, policy gates, on-chain audit trails, multi-chain relay
primitives.cant: Not a CRE workflow by itself — must be wired INTO CRE for the Chainlink bounty; no legal-doc rendering layer yet
primitives.evidence: builder_profile in config.json; leash prod at api.leash.ink [B2]
primitives.load_bearing_for: On-chain policy enforcement + human-readable audit trail = the 'trust layer not the product' spine for any LegalTech/RegTech direction

organizer_feedback.friction: CRE capabilities page does not publish per-capability maturity/beta flags or explicit rate-limit/consensus caveats (e.g. the per-node HTTP fan-out cost); builders must infer limitations
CRE is Go/TS code-first and new (CLI still on rapid 1.2x releases, July 2026); example corpus for LEGAL (non-DeFi) workflows is thin — most CRE examples are price/data feeds, not compliance screening
organizer_feedback.evidence: blog.chain.link/5-ways-to-build-with-cre + field: 7/16 builds reuse the same trading/verdict CRE pattern
